clinician.trajectory_summary: A 51-year-old man presented with symptomatic severe hypercalcemia (>15 mg/dl) manifesting as nausea, vomiting, headache, malaise, and 13 kg weight loss over one month, accompanied by acute kidney injury and appropriately suppressed PTH. Following initial stabilization, CT imaging revealed a 51×47 mm heterogeneous pancreatic mass with calcifications and multiple hypodense liver lesions (largest 73×67 mm in the left lobe). Percutaneous biopsy of the liver mass demonstrated a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor confirmed by immunohistochemistry showing strongly positive chromogranin and synaptophysin, negative CK7, CK20, and LCA, with Ki-67 index <3%. Initial management included hydration, medical therapy, and hemodialysis, resulting in resolution of hypercalcemia (calcium 8.5 mg/dl) and improved renal function (creatinine 1.29 mg/dl) at discharge after 10 days. Long-term management consisted of long-acting octreotide 30 mg monthly and everolimus 10 mg daily after the patient refused surgical intervention (hemi-pancreatectomy and liver transplantation).
